hero.headline: Fork the builders, keep the judges clean
hero.sub: The goal orchestrator was rewritten end to end. Builders inherit the context they already paid for; reviewers never do.

items.title: Builders fork and resume
items.text: An implementer no longer re-explores the codebase from zero on every pass. It forks the session that already read it and continues, so a second round costs a second round — not a second exploration.

items.title: Review stays independent
items.text: Reviewers and validators are dispatched clean, every time. A judge that inherited the builder's context would be marking its own homework.

items.title: Ceremony scales to the goal
items.text: A one-file fix does not get a planning phase, two plan reviewers and a validation gate. A migration does.

blocks.title: What a run looks like
lines: $ claude  →  /goal-skill  add rate limiting to the public API
plan        1 planner        · file-by-file, grounded in the real routes
review      2 lenses         · pragmatist + risk, in parallel  → SOLID
implement   1 builder        · forked from the planner's context
validate    test suite       · the method you agreed to  → PASS
✓ task updated, criteria ticked, progress logged

blocks.text: A validation that is flaky or skipped counts as FAIL. The validator reports the command it ran and its output, so a green result is evidence rather than a claim.

closer.title: How to run one
closer.body: Start a session and invoke /goal-skill with the goal in your own words. It plans, gets the plan critiqued, builds, reviews the code, and validates — and stops to ask when a decision is genuinely yours.
